title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Harvey’s Casino Bombing of 1980
summary: Rerun-style playlist episode on the August 1980 bombing of Harvey's Resort Hotel and Casino in Lake Tahoe, Nevada. A bomb delivered disguised as office equipment was accompanied by a note demanding a $3 million ransom. The FBI bomb squad could not defuse it, the hotel and nearby buildings were evacuated, and after roughly 35 hours a volunteer set off a charge that detonated the device, blowing a large hole in the casino floor. The mastermind, John Waldo Burgess Sr., a gambler with a grudge against Harvey's, was caught after his sons turned on him; he represented himself, was convicted, and died in prison. The episode also covers Harvey Gross's casino history, the failed helicopter money drop, and Burgess's posthumous claim that a loan shark and mob-linked Harvey's executives were behind it, which the hosts dismiss. The episode closes with listener mail about discipline and PBIS.
topics: Stuff You Should Know true crime playlist

segments.title: Cold open
segments.summary: Josh teases the Harvey's Casino bombing as a charming caper in which no one died.

segments.title: Show intro and caper edition
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the true crime edition and the caper theme; the episode was requested by Nick Hales.

segments.title: Bomb delivered to Harvey's and the ransom note
segments.summary: On August 26, 1980, two men delivered a machine marked IBM to Harvey's second-floor offices before dawn. Staff found a note warning that the bomb was extremely sensitive and could not be defused.

segments.title: Bomb sensitivity and ransom demands
segments.summary: The note's detonation details and demands included $3 million in used bills, a helicopter drop at Lake Tahoe Airport, and a demand that news media stay ignorant of the heist. The FBI found about a thousand pounds of dynamite and used the bomb as a training model.

segments.title: Evacuation and media circus
segments.summary: Police evacuated Harvey's and nearby buildings, and the media quickly gathered as the area became a spectacle with betting and souvenir sales.

segments.title: Harvey Gross and early Tahoe casino history
segments.summary: Harvey Gross opened a six-slot-machine cabin in the 1940s in Stateline, Nevada, then expanded to Harvey's Lake Tahoe, an eleven-story building by 1963. The hosts discuss his past run-ins with tax authorities.

segments.title: Gross's background and 1970s crime wave
segments.summary: The hosts describe Gross as not a mob figure and recount his reputation. They tie the 1970s to a wave of kidnappings, ransoms, and hijackings, and mention earlier smoke bomb ransom notes at other Tahoe casinos.

segments.title: Motive revealed and FBI response
segments.summary: The FBI later learned the bombing was a personal vendetta against Harvey's. Special Agent William Jonky proposed a fake payoff to delay the bomb, and Gross offered his own helicopter for the drop.

segments.title: Failed helicopter money drop
segments.summary: An FBI agent piloted Gross's helicopter with a suitcase of mostly fake money. Instructions taped under the payphone sent him on a timed flight; no money drop occurred, and the strobe battery was forgotten.

segments.title: Battery hunt and botched drop site
segments.summary: The conspirators scrambled for a strobe battery, buying one at a gas station after a clerk questioned it. They waited at the drop site 25 miles away, but the helicopter never came.

segments.title: Attempted defusal and the explosion
segments.summary: After the bomb squad considered a switch and then a charge, a volunteer placed a charge about 35 hours after discovery. The charge set off the full bomb, creating a 40 to 50 foot hole. Casino damage was about $18 million, and the casino reopened within days. The bombers' follow-up call to police was an odd moment.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break before discussing the mastermind.

segments.title: John Burgess Sr. background and grudge
segments.summary: John Waldo Burgess Sr. was a gambler and former Luftwaffe pilot with a large gambling debt. He had burned a restaurant for insurance money and was moved out of Harvey's high roller suite, which motivated his revenge.

segments.title: Accomplices Bill Brown and Terry Hall
segments.summary: Bill Brown and Terry Hall delivered the bomb for about $2,100 and learned it was a bomb only after delivery. Burgess Jr. misled them.

segments.title: Bomb construction and hotel clue
segments.summary: The conspirators bought stolen dynamite from a California power plant and built the bomb at home. A night manager, Nancy Domenico, recorded the van's license plate.

segments.title: Tips lead to the Burgess family
segments.summary: John Burgess Jr. bragged to a girlfriend, and after their breakup she told a new boyfriend, who called in a tip. The van was traced to a restaurant Burgess Sr. had burned. Junior claimed he was looking for marijuana planting spots.

segments.title: Arrests, trials, and sentences
segments.summary: After a year of building evidence, the FBI arrested the sons, who cooperated. Ella Williams got seven years, later overturned. Burgess Sr. represented himself, got twenty years federal and life without parole in state prison, and died after 16 years in prison.

segments.title: Posthumous conspiracy claim and Harvey's today
segments.summary: Burgess claimed a loan shark and Harvey's executives and mafia were behind the bombing to collect insurance. The hosts doubt it. Harvey's still operates.

segments.title: Listener mail on discipline and PBIS
segments.summary: A third-grade teacher shares PBIS, a praise-and-reward behavior method, and Chuck considers trying it at home.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits and iHeartRadio promotion.
